expected: the Jevellan web app "git settings" screen at phone-dark, rendered completely and legibly (one of several screens captured during "Git settings can be saved, reloaded and checked from Projects"; the other steps are judged in their own screenshots)

cosmetic: The settings tab strip clips its labels at both edges ("ices" on the left, a partly hidden tab after "Ekoa" on the right). Scroll arrows are shown, so the tabs can still be reached.
The 'Save Git settings' button has very low contrast. That fits a disabled state, but it is hard to see against the dark card.
The 'GitHub token scope' label and dropdown sit outside any card, unlike the other sections, so the layout looks inconsistent.
The helper text under 'Use SSH for GitHub' is small and low-contrast grey, though still readable.
The long repository path wraps in the middle of a word ('activity-context-' / 'origin.git'). It is still fully readable.
